thread:
Marta: Quick run: perf + flamegraph on CPU-side during a heavy serving workload. Found unexpected Python hotspots around tokenization and the request scheduler. Sharing commands, results, and a couple of micro-experiments.

Devin: drop the perf command and high-level config (model, batch mix)? also curious about QPS.

Marta: infra: 8xA100 worker pool, model=gpt-medium-open, batch distribution 40% size=1, 30% size=2, 20% size=4, 10% size=8. Steady ~1.2k req/s.

Marta: perf workflow I used:
```
perf record -F 99 -p <worker_pid> -g -- sleep 60
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```

Marta: perf top (trimmed):
```
Samples: 12803 of event 'cpu-clock'
  19.6% python  [.] PyEval_EvalFrameEx
  11.4% python  [.] tokenize_bytes
  10.1% python  [.] scheduler::drain_queue
   6.2% libc    [.] pthread_cond_wait
   4.9% python  [.] kv_cache_lookup
```

Claire: tokenize_bytes that high is surprising. Are we hitting fallback Python paths for some encodings/input shapes?

Marta: yes — found ~7% of requests hit a non-utf8 branch that routes through a slow Python routine. Microbench: that codepath is ~4x slower than C tokenizer.

Devin: scheduler::drain_queue at 10% implies per-request coordination costs. Can you paste top stacks (collapsed) so we can see the callers?

Marta: top stacks (collapsed):
```
python PyEval_EvalFrameEx;tokenize_bytes;handle_special_chars
python PyEval_EvalFrameEx;scheduler::drain_queue;batch_builder::try_emit
python PyEval_EvalFrameEx;kv_cache_lookup;dict_getitem;hash_lookup
libc pthread_cond_wait;runtime::cond_wait;wait_loop
```

Sam: two quick hypotheses: (1) tokenization fallback causing GIL-bound work; (2) frequent cross-thread wakeups for batching causing syscall churn.

Marta: to test (1) I toggled a C tokenizer extension behind a flag for 5 minutes. Results (median over windows):
- python tokenizer: p50=24ms p95=128ms
- C tokenizer: p50=19ms p95=92ms
CPU usage on worker process fell by ~8%.

Claire: decent tail improvement but p95 still high. Did you collect sched event traces (wakeups / context switches)?

Marta: yes. I recorded sched wakeups and switches and aggregated stacks:
```
wakeups in 60s: 164k (avg ~4.1 wakeups per request)
common wakeup stack:
  runtime::notify -> epoll_wait -> write -> eventfd_write
```

Devin: that implicates our batching flush/coordination. If we flush aggressively for latency, we pay inter-thread signals. Consider an adaptive short timer to allow small coalescing windows when concurrency is high.

Sam: also consider eliminating the pipe/eventfd handoff by using per-core queues + single-writer handoff to the batcher to avoid cross-thread wakeups.

Marta: implemented quick PoC: spin-then-yield strategy — spin up to 200us waiting for additional items, then fallback to condvar wake. Ran with same workload: wakeups dropped ~47%.

Marta: new perf top after PoC:
```
  PyEval_EvalFrameEx 13.0%
  tokenize_bytes       7.0%
  scheduler::drain_queue 5.0%
  pthread_cond_wait   11.6%
```

Marta: latency improved: p50=18ms p95=78ms. CPU-per-request decreased ~10%. Flamegraph shows much smaller Python stacks for tokenization and scheduler.

Devin: nice. Two follow-ups: (A) roll out C tokenizer behind an opt-in flag across canary hosts; (B) experiment with adaptive batching timer (e.g., 5-15ms window depending on concurrency) and measure tail impact. I'll add the eval infra job to run across other batch mixes.

Claire: one more hotspot to watch: kv_cache_lookup at ~5% originally. Python dict lookups are generally cheap but our access pattern creates temporary allocations/boxing. Any plan?

Marta: prototyped a small C shim for hot-prefix lookups (keeps PyObject* keys and returns borrowed references). Microbench shows ~2.5x improvement on our hot path. Will gate behind feature flag.

Sam: plan sounds good. Make sure to capture memory/regression tests; C shim needs strict refcounting checks. Also validate on multi-tenant load.

Marta: will attach out.folded (before/after) and flame.svg to PERF ticket. Also saved perf.data and the sched aggregation script.

Devin: please include the commands and exact PID mapping in the ticket so SRE can reproduce. I'll wire up an automated perf job for different batch mixes (1/2/4 heavy).

Marta: done. Files uploaded to ticket #5421. Thanks for feedback! :pray:

ops-bot: Incident logged: PERF-2026-118 1 linked ticket #5421 (CPU tokenization + scheduler investigation).

Sam: overall nice incremental wins. Next steps: canary C tokenizer + C cache shim, iterate on adaptive batching timer, and run 24h p95 monitoring post-rollout.

Marta: agreed. I'll open a short RFC for the batching heuristic change and a rollout checklist.

Claire: +1 to RFC. Also include unit tests for the tokenizer's edge branches so we can reduce fallback rate.

Marta: will add tests. Thanks all.
